subject: FinLytics: cascading retries & elevated 5xx/429 after model-v2b quant rollout
messages:
From: Jorge Alvarez <jorge@finlytics.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@finlytics.com
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 09:12:27 -0800
Subject: Urgent - production timeouts & 5xx/429 spike after your model change

Monica / Laura —

We started seeing a large spike in 429 and 5xx errors in our checkout microservice starting ~08:45 PST right after the scheduled rollout of model-v2b (quantized profile v3) that Redwood performed for our account. Traffic is now seeing cascading retries from our side and latency has doubled for the tokenization step. Our SREs are seeing the backend request timeout at ~1.8s (was 350ms).

Attached is a snapshot of our SLO dashboard (slo_dashboard.png) and a small sample of error logs (error_sample.log). Can you confirm whether you rolled a quant/profile or kernel update for finlytics-prod today? We need this contained — business is impacted.

Please escalate.

— Jorge
Head of Platform, FinLytics

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, aditya.rao@redwood.ai, hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 09:34:05 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Urgent - production timeouts & 5xx/429 spike after your model change

Quick triage notes (initial):
- I see a rollout job at 08:36 that pushed model-v2b with quant-profile v3 to the us-west-2 hosted pool for FinLytics (rollout ID: roll-20270110-78).
- Kernel telemetry shows a new fused-attn kernel was enabled for that model variant at 08:35. We have degrading tail-latency for sequences >256 tokens on a subset of instances (p95->p99 increased; CPU offload and memcpy patterns changed).
- Error pattern: many requests are hitting an internal inference timeout (configured 1.5s for that route) then client-side retries increase QPS, producing 429s upstream as our admission controller tries to protect overloaded workers. Logs show a handful of OOM-with-retry exceptions on a small fraction of hosts.

Suggested immediate mitigations (order matters):
1) Revert the fused-attn kernel toggle for roll-20270110-78 (quick flip in kernel feature flag).
2) Increase per-request timeout on the FinLytics route to 3s to reduce client-side retry amplification while we stabilize (short term).
3) Schedule a hot rollback of roll-20270110-78 if kernel flip revert does not reduce error rate in 10m.

I can flip the kernel flag in ~4 minutes. Need agreement on timeout change — Laura can you confirm if FinLytics will accept a temporary per-request latency bump?

— Rishi
SRE Lead, Serving Runtime

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jorge Alvarez <jorge@finlytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 09:40:44 -08:00
Subject: Re: Urgent - production timeouts & 5xx/429 spike after your model change

Jorge — thanks for the quick flag. We see the same. Monica & team are triaging and have a mitigation plan. Short answer: yes, we had a scheduled rollout that included a quant-profile update and we are treating this as a high-priority incident.

We will:
- Attempt a kernel toggle revert immediately (Rishi is on this).
- If we need longer time, we will increase the route timeout temporarily and coordinate a hot rollback.

I'll keep you updated every 15 minutes and share a timeline for the rollback if needed. Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts checkout conversions.

— Laura

laura.bennett@redwood.ai | +1 650-555-0189

From: aditya.rao@redwood.ai

Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 09:47:51 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Urgent - production timeouts & 5xx/429 spike after your model change

I flipped the kernel feature flag for roll-20270110-78 at 09:46:30 (action id act-20270110-322). Early indicators: 60% reduction in p99 tail latency on the affected cohort; 5xx rate down 45% in the first 3 minutes. No new OOMs reported on hosts we observed.

Next steps I recommend:
- Keep the temporary route timeout at 3s for 30m while we monitor for retry amplification.
- Start a controlled rollback plan (hot rollback) to model-v2a in case residual errors remain beyond 20m. Rollback playbook (link in related_links) is ready.
- Rishi: please surface any host-level remediation if OOMs reoccur (kernel change might have widened memory usage distribution).

I'll continue to stream logs to the incident channel.

— Aditya
Infra Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Jorge Alvarez <jorge@finlytics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai, hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 14:03:02 -08:00
Subject: RE: Urgent - production timeouts & 5xx/429 spike after your model change

Jorge — quick update and next steps: we identified the regression caused by the fused-attn kernel toggle that accompanied quant-profile v3 for model-v2b. Our infra team reverted the kernel flag at 09:46 PST and saw immediate improvement; 5xxs are down ~70% and 429s are decreasing as admission control heals.

Temporary mitigations in place now:
- Kernel toggle reverted (completed).
- Per-route timeout increased to 3s for 30 minutes to prevent client retry amplification.
- We have not yet performed a full hot rollback to v2a; that will be executed if error rate does not stabilize within the next 30 minutes.

Action items for next 48 hours:
- Rishi & Hannah: postmortem to include kernel compatibility checklist and an expanded pre-roll Q/A for quantized profiles (including longer tail-latency sampling).
- Aditya: prepare a staged Canary test (smaller pop) for re-rolling v2b with a conservative kernel build and updated memory margins.
- Laura: coordinate with FinLytics SREs on client-side retry backoff tuning; we will provide a recommended short-term policy.

We apologize for the disruption. I will keep you posted and will set a 1:00pm PST follow-up to share post-stabilization findings and next steps.

— Monica
